title: LeBron James sues AI sports-betting analytics app over alleged bogus endorsement
excerpt: Lebron James sued PlayVision, alleging the company stole his name and likeness to make consumers believe he endorsed a sports-betting analytics app.
content_html:
By Natalie Musumeci

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-17T22:01:23.054Z

NBA legend LeBron James is taking an AI sports-betting analytics app dubbed Bron to court, accusing the startup behind the tool of stealing his name and likeness to make consumers believe he endorsed it.

James' lawsuit, filed Tuesday in Manhattan federal court by celebrity attorney Alex Spiro, alleges that PlayVision, the Y Combinator-backed company behind the app, illegally traded on the basketball star's identity to unjustly enrich itself.

"Defendants selected the name 'Bron' precisely to evoke Mr. James, to trade on his fame and goodwill, and to falsely suggest to the public that Mr. James endorsed or was affiliated with the Bron App," the lawsuit says.

In addition to PlayVision, the company's founders, Mark Zogby and Anish Gupta — the CEO — are also named as defendants in the lawsuit. Representatives for PlayVision did not immediately respond to a request for comment by Business Insider.

The lawsuit points to a November advertisement that it says was built around an AI-generated version of James in a No. 23 jersey bearing his "Bron" nickname and sporting tattoos that mimicked his.

"Speaking in Mr. James's voice, the AI-generated Mr. James scrolls through wagers on other NBA players in Defendants' Bron App. The Ad then urges viewers to 'Scroll to bet,'" says the lawsuit, which alleges trademark infringement.

The ad "catapulted the Bron App from obscurity to controversy, with the Ad gaining a million views within a day—exactly as Defendants intended. But Mr. James has no affiliation with Defendants or their product," the lawsuit says.

The complaint alleges that the defendants violated James' rights and treated the violation as a "marketing expense."

When James' attorneys sent the company a cease-and-desist letter, the lawsuit says the startup used it as an opportunity to "gin up additional publicity, taking down the Ad while teasing 'a new name' without delivering one and daring Mr. James to file a lawsuit."

The lawsuit, which seeks a jury trial and an unspecified amount of monetary damages, said James is "one of the most recognizable identities in the world" and that he commands tens of millions of dollars in fees for endorsing a product or venture.

"His endorsement is uniquely valuable," the lawsuit says. "And that is why Defendants decided to steal it all for themselves."
